brands.name: Velzy Surfboards
brands.short_description: Heritage surfboards from Dale "Hawk" Velzy — the San Clemente shaper who opened the world's first surf shop in 1950 and invented the pig design that changed how the world rides waves.

models.name: Pig
models.description: In the post-WWII surf scene, Dale Velzy narrowed the nose of a balsa blank, moved the wide point back from center/forward by 8–10 inches, and gave the aft end a major tail-block. The Pig was born — greater maneuverability in the pocket and increased hold for noseriding. Overnight, hotdogging entered the surfer's vernacular and riding waves would never be the same.

In 1966, the act of noseriding was the reason for the season. As a partnership, Hap Jacobs and Dale Velzy entered the fray with their own apparatus: the 422. This reverse-rocker tip time machine features a deep concave that extends almost three-quarters the length of the board, with a unique rail bump and step-tail that increases maneuverability in and out of steep sections.

models.name: Malibu Express
models.description: "Simmons made them light; I made them turn" – Dale Velzy. The Malibu Express lives up to its moniker: a speed demon with flat, continuous rocker, a sleek pintail outline, subtle hull entry with roll, center, and vee in front of the fin, and pinched 50/50 rails from nose to tail. Dale always said surfboards work best closest to the living curl — the Express thrives in steep sections.
